title: Global existence and the uniform a priori estimate in homogeneous Besov spaces for the 2D inviscid magnetic Benard system (Theorem 1.1)
author: Hao Liu; Ruixin Zeng; Chengrong Zhang
work: Nonlinear stability and optimal decay rates of inviscid magnetic Benard fluids
source_version: Electronic Journal of Differential Equations 2026, No. 17, pp. 1--15; DOI 10.58997/ejde.2026.17; publisher version
difficulty_reason: After the paper's Section 2 toolkit (Littlewood--Paley decomposition, Bernstein inequalities, Besov embedding, interpolation and derivative properties, product and commutator estimates) is supplied as context, the counted proof still has to build a source-local mechanism. It must first extract a horizontal dissipation term for the velocity from the temperature equation and a vertical dissipation term from the magnetic equation, through the cancellation identities (3.4), (3.6), (3.7) and (3.8) (source lines 544--609); then combine those four frequency-localized identities with two large constants C1 and C2 into the augmented energy functionals and prove their coercivity against the negative cross terms by Bernstein inequality in the two frequency regimes j at most 0 and j at least -1 (lines 611--666 and 729--777); then sum over the dyadic blocks in the two Besov norms and bound every nonlinear and commutator term by the product of the two energy functionals (lines 677--693 and 850--884); and finally close the Lyapunov-type differential inequality (3.26) under the smallness condition on the supremum of the energy, which is what forces the life span to be infinite by the bootstrap argument (lines 887--908). The named analytic ingredients are classical, but their assembly here is paper-specific and coercivity-free: the dissipation is recovered only from the coupling structure, the two frequency regimes require an induction that is made self-consistent through the constants C1 and C2, and the resulting estimate is uniform in the life span. That is clearly beyond an ordinary PhD qualifying examination on the Euler, Navier--Stokes or MHD equations, and it is graded H2 rather than H3 because each individual ingredient is a named classical estimate rather than a new research device.
